newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Belgian foreign minister meets Pakistan president.
newsitem.headline: Belgian foreign minister meets Pakistan president.

text.p: Visiting Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke held talks with Pakistani President Farooq Leghari on Thursday, a Belgian diplomat said.

Scheduled talks with newly elected Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, who has yet to name his cabinet, did not take place. Since Pakistan has no foreign minister at present, Derycke met Najmuddin Sheikh, secretary at the foreign ministry, instead.

Derycke, the first foreign minister to visit Pakistan since Sharif romped to power in February 3 general elections, earlier visited the Khyber Pass, transit route for opium that is grown in Afghanistan, processed into heroin and smuggled to Europe.
Derycke spent 90 minutes with Leghari, who called the elections after dismissing Benazir Bhutto's government on disputed charges of corruption and misrule on November 5.
The Belgian foreign minister, the first to come to Pakistan since 1987, has said he is keen to boost economic and trade relations. Bilateral trade is now worth nearly $300 million.
He also briefed his hosts on Belgium's concern about disarmament ahead of a special conference to promote a ban on anti-personnel mines to be held in Brussels in June.
Derycke, who arrived in Islamabad on Wednesday night, was due to fly home early on Friday, the diplomat said.
